source_documents.title: New Naphthalimide Derivative as a Colorimetric and Fluorescent Probe for Detection of pH, Strong Bases and Volatile Acids

reference_evidence_units.quote: (quenched fluorescence) due to the presence of PET from the tertiary nitrogen atom from the N,N-dimethylamine group in the side chain of the molecule.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Designed off state: PET from the dimethylamino receptor.

reference_evidence_units.quote: were observed in the solvents with small polarity, as well as an absence of fluorescence in the solvents with high polarity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 5

reference_evidence_units.quote: the molecule may undergo a hypso- or bathochromic color shift as a result of the reduction or enhancement in the efficiency of the ICT from the donor moiety (the secondary nitrogen atom from the imino group at the C-4 position of the naphthalimide) to the acceptor moiety (the carbonyl group of the naphthalimide).
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 5
reference_evidence_units.statement: Colour changes come from ICT of the 4-amino-naphthalimide.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Using the protonation of the secondary amine, directly attached to the naphthalimide and the tertiary amine in the side chain, in the presence of acids and their vapors, not only in solution, but also in the thin film and strip paper, the compound shows a considerable hypsochromic shift in color and strong fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 5 + acid
